claims.text: The rider's claim is proven on the platform's own trace: the GPS polyline between the recorded pickup and dropoff events measures 14.44 km against a booked optimal of 12.0 km, an excess of 2.44 km. That excess is 20.33% of optimal, which clears the 20% limb of POL-RD-01, and 2.44 km clears the 0.8 km absolute limb. Both establishment tests pass, so the deviation is ESTABLISHED and the outcome cannot be NO_ACTION.

The governing distance figure is the trace, not the trip record. POL-RD-01 says gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs where the two disagree, and here the trace reads 14.44 km while trip_record.actual_distance_km reads 14.4 km. The trace figure is the one that must be used for the threshold test, and it is the one that establishes the excess.

The rider has discharged the initial burden under POL-RD-08. The trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry the same trip identifier TRP-02842 and the same pickup/start window (trip started 2026-08-24T06:34:18+08:00, first GPS fix 2026-08-24T06:34:18+08:00), and the excess of 2.44 km meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The burden therefore shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and clause.

The driver's excuse — 'Minor detour because of a road works sign' — carries no weight. POL-RD-13 tests an asserted external traffic cause against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else, and the bundle holds no advisory covering this trip window: EV-ADVIS-02842-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload. POL-RD-03 is therefore unavailable, the assertion is discarded under POL-RD-08, and the deviation stands at the measured figure.

The driver's road-works assertion cites no evidence ID for any advisory, so the missing advisory is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact within POL-RD-10(5). Under POL-RD-13(1) an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one, and the absence of an artifact no party has cited is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it. This case does not escalate on that ground.

No rider-requested detour can excuse any part of the excess. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction recorded in the chat_log, and the chat log for this trip is empty: message_count 0, no messages, first and last message timestamps null. With no instruction on file, POL-RD-04 is unavailable and no distance is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied.

No relocation of the pickup or dropoff point can excuse the excess either. POL-RD-05 requires an amendment after booking, and the trip_record shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null, with amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min both null. The clause cannot be run and the booked optimal of 12.0 km stands as the baseline.

This is not a pooled trip, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. The trip_record records vehicle_type RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null. The baseline for POL-RD-01 is therefore the ordinary booked optimal of 12.0 km, and the whole 2.44 km excess counts against the driver.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 and the fare model is METERED, so the clause runs. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 12.0 + 0.28 x 16.0) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP = (3.80 + 9.00 + 4.48) + 0.80 = 18.08. Charged_total is 20.66, so the refund is 20.66 - 18.08 = 2.58, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, i.e. SGD 2.60. The surge multiplier of 1.0 is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, not from the trip_record.

The refund is not de minimis and does not reach the full-refund share. The computed refund of SGD 2.60 is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so NO_ACTION does not apply; and it is 12.49% of charged_total, far below the 90% full_refund_share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND rather than FULL_REFUND.

No ERP or surcharge correction is due. The fare_breakdown carries zero ERP lines (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.0, off_optimal_route_total 0.00) and no airport surcharge (airport_surcharge 0.0), and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport. There is no phantom gantry line and no billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4), and under POL-RD-09(1) any off-route ERP would in any event already be comprehended in the POL-RD-02 figure and could not be added on top of it.

The driver's profile does not establish a repeat-deviation pattern, and I do not press one. POL-RD-06 requires driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d of 3 or more, or a ratio of 0.05 or more against completed_trips_90d of at least 40. Here deviation_flags_90d is 0 and completed_trips_90d is 396, so the ratio is 0.0. No pattern is established, no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) is available, and no conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) follows. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags (1) is not the trailing-90-day figure this clause asks for and may not be substituted for it.

The rider's profile does not trigger the extra corroboration requirement. POL-RD-08 raises the bar only where rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1 or fewer; here both are 0, so the claim needs no corroboration beyond the trace. The rider's other profile fields (rating, account_age_days, lifetime_trips) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and ground no finding.

The trace is clean for policy purposes and no escalation trigger fires. The GPS artifact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with 100.0% coverage, 114 fixes at a 10 s interval, zero gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0, so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) are not met and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. Trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, timestamps do not run backwards, the refund of SGD 2.60 is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling and below charged_total, and no charge line lacks a counterpart. The case is decidable on the record.

1. Was the route longer than it should have been? The platform's own GPS trace (EV-GPS-02842) measures the route actually driven at 14.44 km between the recorded pickup at 06:34:18 and the recorded dropoff at 06:53:08. The booked optimal route (EV-TRIP-02842) is 12.0 km. That is an excess of 2.44 km, or 20.33% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH tests: more than 0.8 km absolute (2.44 km — passed) and more than 20% of optimal (20.33% — passed, but only just). The trace figure governs, not the rounded 14.4 km on the trip record. The deviation is established. It is not a MATERIAL deviation (under 50% and under 8.0 km), so no POL-RD-06 pattern check or uplift arises.

2. The driver's explanation. The driver says the detour was minor and caused by a road-works sign. POL-RD-13 tests that against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. The only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-02842-01, is MISSING: status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, no payload, because no advisory covered this corridor in this window. POL-RD-03 cannot be run — no road is named, no validity window can be compared, no alternative distance exists to cap an exoneration — so the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and the excess is not reduced. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes (114 fixes, 10 s interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps, max gap 0.0 s), so nothing needs corroborating it under POL-RD-07.

Your explanation, Driver, that there was 'a minor detour because of a road works sign', does not reduce the excess. It is an asserted external traffic cause, and POL-RD-13 tests such an assertion against the traffic advisory for this trip and nothing else. The bundle's only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-02842-01, is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, no payload), so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run, no shortest lawful alternative distance exists to cap any exoneration, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Because you named no advisory evidence ID, the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle rather than the contradiction POL-RD-10(5) escalates on, so no escalation issues on that ground; the absence is itself citable but carries no fact (POL-GEN-02(3)).

No other excuse is open. The chat log EV-CHAT-02842 holds zero messages, so no rider-requested detour can be made out under POL-RD-04. The trip record shows no pickup or dropoff amendment (both timestamps null, amended optimal null), so POL-RD-05 cannot run. The vehicle is RYDE_X rather than RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not displace the 12.0 km baseline. The deviation is not material (20.33% is below 50% and 2.44 km is below 8.0 km), and the driver profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against 396 completed trips in 90 days, so there is no repeat-pattern uplift and no conduct referral under POL-RD-06. Profile fields such as prior_deviation_flags, rating and account age are context only under POL-GEN-01 and were not used as grounds for anything.

That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and is 12.5% of charged_total, far below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 2.60 to the rider. You put the overcharge at SGD 2.00, Rider; POL-RD-02 makes the refund arithmetic rather than discretionary, and the figures give SGD 2.60. The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines and no airport surcharge, so POL-RD-09 has nothing to add on top of that figure.

All three deciding artifacts - GPS trace, trip record and fare breakdown - sit at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0; confidence is set at 0.95 because the excess clears the 20% limb by a narrow margin. The monetary effect of SGD 2.60 is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically on issue, subject to the appeal route under POL-GEN-04.
